To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) we propose a novel structured vector model for word meaning in context, and (2) the model outperforms existing models on the task of paraphrase adequacy.

(1) the selectional preferences of a word’s arguments can be used to improve the quality of vector space models of word meaning in contexts; (2) the resulting model can be used to compute the contextual adequacy scores of word paraphrases; and (3) the model outperforms the state of the arts in the latter task.

(i) the selectional preferences of a verb are a function of its arguments; (ii) the model is able to predict the selectional preferences from the verb’s argument positions; (iii) the model can be used to predict the selection of arguments by verbs, and to model the contextual adequacy and paraphrase relations of word occurrences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the meaning of individual words in context.
the question of how to model the meaning of words in context, and we argue that the answer lies in the combination of syntactic and distributional information.
the question of how to best represent the meaning of a word in context, given the syntactic structure of the sentence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model presented here is the first model of word meaning in a vector space that is both syntactically informed and empirically successful.

our model is a significant advance in the state of the-art for the task of modeling the meaning of words in context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a model for word meaning in context that incorporates syntax, is able to capture the contextual adequacy for paraphrase, and performs well on the standard tasks of word similarity and analogy.
we propose a novel model for word meaning that takes into account both syntax and semantics and we show that our model performs well for both tasks.

we propose a new structured vector space model for word meaning in context and demonstrate its effectiveness in modeling the contextual adequacies of paraphrases and the selectional preferences of word arguments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
syntactic information is crucial for modeling the contextual meaning of words.
a simple model that incorporates selectional preferences for word senses can achieve state-of-the-art results on word sense disambiguation.
the syntactic structure of sentences is crucial for modeling the contextual meaning of words.
